Record version: 1.0. Owner: fixture author. Recorded: 2026-11-23. Status: attributed public background, not operating authority. All business records, people, dialogue and account identifiers in this dossier are synthetic.

S01: The official REWORK Live episode dated January 24, 2024 contains a pricing discussion beginning at 00:53:37. Jason Fried described a long practice of leaving existing customers on older prices, followed by a roughly twenty percent increase for some legacy products or existing customers with about ninety days of notice. He attributed the change to higher costs. These are company statements about its pricing decision, not independent evidence of any particular customer's notice receipt or contractual rights.

S02: Jason Fried's October 9, 2008 Signal v. Noise post about product pricing discusses adjusting prices and recommends ample warning, considering grandfathering longer-term customers, and explaining benefits. This is first-party business commentary, not an executed customer promise, a universal notice rule, or evidence that every later subscriber obtained a permanent rate guarantee.

S03: The 37signals terms page retrieved on November 23, 2026 displays a November 12, 2026 update. Its pricing section says existing customers tend to be exempted from price changes but can have prices changed with at least thirty days of notice to the recorded email address. This current wording does not establish the company's terms in 2008 or 2024, a particular customer's receipt, or the fictional contract below.

These three distinct primary records ground the tension between an established expectation and a later pricing decision. Their dates and scopes differ. No source establishes that a particular grandfathering representation is enforceable forever, that any given notice was received, or that a customer agreed to a replacement plan. The fixture includes original factual paraphrases only. No transcript, audio, screenshot, source-page dump, actual customer domain or personal contact information is reproduced. No open transcript redistribution license is asserted. Local paragraph hashes in the source registry identify the authored representations, not original webpages.

NacreFlow and Rookfield Planning Cooperative are fictional. The decision cutoff is June 27, 2025 at 14:00 UTC, before a July 1 annual renewal. Neither the public sources nor their later dates supply fictional knowledge at that cutoff. Historical pricing examples motivate the business problem; dated fictional orders, authority records, system states and customer communications determine what staff can responsibly communicate or execute. The account is not in a historical litigation or a real company's billing system. The synthetic figures intentionally differ from the public examples.

Rookfield uses a collaborative planning product for paid professional work. Its dispute concerns Core40 pricing, an old sales assurance, notice, and who can elect a renewal while the board considers alternatives. Some attachments are stale and some current messages have limited authority; retaining those distinctions is necessary to understand the business records.
# E02 — Executed Core40 order and incorporated terms

Record version: ORDER-2022.1. Owner: NacreFlow Contracts. Signed: 2022-06-15. Current annual term: 2024-07-01 through 2025-07-01 00:00 UTC. Status: executed order and renewal record. All business records, people, dialogue and account identifiers in this dossier are synthetic.

Rookfield Planning Cooperative subscribes to Core40: forty named staff accounts, shared project workspaces, external read-only reviewers, scheduled exports and the standard integration API. Its annual subscription is $9,600 excluding tax, payable in advance. Core40's annual price is expressed as forty seats at $240 per seat per year. The original order does not offer an unlimited headcount plan. Extra staff require a separately accepted quantity change. External reviewers do not consume paid staff seats while restricted to read-only review.

The order names Miri Bell, Rookfield finance director, as commercial signatory and Noor Hale as operational administrator. Miri can accept subscription amendments, change financial contacts and appoint a limited delegate in writing. Noor can manage workspaces, exports and members within the purchased quantity. The role table alone gives Noor no general power to accept a new annual commitment or settle a dispute. A separately recorded delegation can confer narrower power; staff must check its scope and whether later instructions limit it. Board approval is Rookfield's internal governance, not a general requirement NacreFlow imposed on every renewal.

Annual renewal occurs automatically for the same service quantity unless a valid nonrenewal instruction or recorded provider gate intervenes. The order's notice address is the billing contact recorded in the customer profile. A renewal price increase requires sixty calendar days' advance written notice to that address. Price changes do not apply during a paid annual term. The account-specific price schedule takes precedence over inconsistent general pricing pages for that term. Material modifications to negotiated terms require signatures from authorized representatives of both parties. Silence after a website update is not stated to be a signature.

The signed order identifies the service description and standard terms as attachments. Its index lists a one-page implementation acceptance certificate and an introductory price schedule. It does not list a permanent-price side letter by filename. Rookfield supplied a separate sales attachment this week; NacreFlow's archive also contains it. The archive's failure to list it on the order index is evidence of a documentation gap, not proof that the attachment is fabricated. Its language and signatures appear in E03 and E04.

Renewals in 2023 and 2024 used Core40 at $9,600. No eight-seat expansion has been executed. The new standardized annual Core40 price would be $14,400, forty seats at $360, from a qualifying renewal. The proposed difference is $4,800 a year, a fifty percent increase. Taxes are not included in these comparisons. No usage charges, historical debt, implementation fees or service-credit balance are at issue. Any route must keep the current paid term separate from a future price, an unaccepted expansion and a temporary service extension.
# E03 — Archived sales assurance and customer reliance

Record version: SALES-2022.2. Owner: Sales Operations archive. Original exchange: 2022-06-13. Archive assembled: 2025-06-26 10:20 UTC. Status: authentic archived correspondence; legal scope unresolved. All business records, people, dialogue and account identifiers in this dossier are synthetic.

Sales representative Ava Lorne sent Miri a follow-up two days before the original signature. Ava described Core40 as a stable home for the cooperative and wrote, in this synthetic exchange, that Rookfield's forty-seat base rate would stay at $9,600 while the account remained continuously subscribed to Core40; annual review would cover additional seats or new capabilities. The message linked the price schedule and attached a page titled founding customer rate assurance. The wording was broader than a one-year introductory discount. It did not promise that all future products would be included or that additional seats would be free.

Miri replied that the stable base price was a material reason to choose NacreFlow over an annual tender process. She explained that clients budgeted on multi-year planning cycles. Ava acknowledged that point and asked her to sign the order before implementation began. Rookfield's original procurement worksheet compares a $9,600 recurring cost against two competitors' first-year costs. The worksheet has a note about avoiding future base-price uncertainty. That note supports reliance as a customer position; it does not prove the sales representative had every required power.

The attachment is a native PDF whose text matches the archived email attachment checksum. Its footer says account-specific sales assurance, not a general marketing advertisement. Ava signed it as account executive; Miri signed as customer finance director. The wording makes continued Core40 subscription a condition. It contains no minimum annual spend beyond the forty-seat price and no expressly stated end date. It also does not define what happens if the company replaces the product name while retaining essentially the same service. No such replacement has been announced in this account's current notice.

Ava is no longer employed by NacreFlow. Sales Operations has not contacted her and cannot supply her present interpretation. The fixture contains no allegation that she forged anything. The archive associates the attachment with the deal but does not record an exception number or finance countersignature for an indefinite price commitment. The sales compensation record shows credit for a standard annual sale. Neither the compensation code nor the absence of a special code establishes all contract effects.

The current customer asks NacreFlow to address the actual assurance rather than describe it as a generic discount that naturally expired. Rookfield has not demanded that additional seats or new optional modules retain 2022 prices. Its claim is narrower: the same forty-seat service should not become fifty percent more expensive merely because the published pricing page changed. Support's prior shorthand that grandfathering ended everywhere does not answer that claim. The account history and signature records must be reconciled with the present approval process before staff can promise a permanent outcome.
# E04 — Historical and current signatory register

Record version: AUTH-2022.4. Owner: Corporate Secretary. Register snapshot: 2025-06-27 13:15 UTC. Status: historical delegation and signature scope; not a new decision. All business records, people, dialogue and account identifiers in this dossier are synthetic.

In June 2022, an account executive could issue the approved annual price schedule and offer a first-term discount up to twenty percent. A regional sales manager could approve a discount for the current annual term. An indefinite price lock, a variation of renewal-price provisions, or a commitment lasting more than two years required the chief commercial officer and finance director jointly. Regional manager Petra Venn signed the implementation acceptance certificate on June 16, 2022. The certificate confirms readiness of onboarding resources and approval of the commercial configuration in order NF-2240. Its signature field is headed delivery and first-term commercial approval. A checkbox states price schedule reviewed. The certificate does not reproduce the rate-assurance wording. Rookfield retained it alongside Ava's assurance; Miri reads Petra's signature as company confirmation of the whole deal. Contracts staff read the certificate as confirming the implementation and first annual term. Neither view changes the words that the certificate actually contains.

The historical register was internal. The customer did not receive a copy in 2022. Counsel has cautioned that internal delegation limits and the effect of customer-facing representations are related but different questions. The register identifies who may authorize today's concessions; it is not itself a final adjudication of apparent authority, incorporation or reasonable reliance. Staff should not tell the customer that a representation is automatically void simply because a salesperson lacked an internal code. They also should not represent that Petra expressly approved a permanent price when the signature scope does not say that.

The current authority schedule, AUTH-2025.1, took effect April 1, 2025. Support associates may explain records and coordinate a case. Duty support leads may establish a manual renewal gate before the batch runs, deferring the scheduled renewal for up to seven calendar days beyond the paid boundary and preserving existing service during that extension without an additional charge. This delegation changes processing and short continuity, not the permanent negotiated price or the customer's election. Finance Operations can alter a draft invoice once a financial approval and any required acceptance are attached. It cannot create a perpetual price exception or use a renewal gate as a cancellation instruction.

Finance director Sela Moss may approve up to one additional annual Core40 term at the legacy price, or a paid bridge up to three calendar months at the corresponding legacy monthly rate. She cannot approve a permanent price guarantee, a waiver of all claims, or an unpriced forty-eight-seat account. Joint executive and legal review would be needed for a new indefinite commitment or a formal dispute settlement. The June 27 case-specific decision in E15 is distinct from this general delegation. All staff must use its actual conditions rather than infer approval from a title alone.
# E05 — Superseded grandfathering operations guide

Record version: LEGACY-2023.3. Owner: Revenue Operations. Effective: 2023-01-01. Superseded for new decisions: 2025-04-01. Status: archived procedure; retained to explain historical actions. All business records, people, dialogue and account identifiers in this dossier are synthetic.

The 2023 operations guide instructed billing staff to retain the founding-price flag on continuously subscribed legacy accounts. Core40 renewals carrying that flag would use the last accepted annual amount, absent a quantity change. The guide was created to prevent accidental increases after a pricing-page redesign. It was an internal processing rule, not a customer contract and not an independent source of indefinite signatory power. It did not direct staff to audit every legacy promise before every renewal.

The guide allowed a billing specialist to restore a missing legacy flag when the previous paid invoice and account continuity matched. The specialist needed an audit note and manager acknowledgment. This restoration did not require a new contract because it preserved the then-configured renewal amount. Commercial staff often summarized this as existing customers stay on their rate. The customer-facing help card used the phrase founding customers keep their price, with a small note that quantity and plan changes might alter the bill. The card has no current effective date and should not be sent as today's complete rule.

In July 2023, Rookfield's legacy flag survived a database migration. In July 2024, an analyst checked continuous subscription and renewed at $9,600 without obtaining a new exception approval. Those actions explain why Rookfield saw two years of consistent treatment after the original assurance. They also limit what the internal record proves: the analyst did not investigate whether Ava's letter bound the company forever. The absence of a fresh approval on each renewal is consistent with the old operations procedure.

The archived guide has a section about account interruption. A customer that canceled its subscription and later returned would ordinarily move to then-current pricing, while a brief payment-processing error could be corrected without losing legacy status. Rookfield has had neither a cancellation nor a service gap. The sales team suggested that an unsuccessful automatic debit might cause loss of grandfathering; nothing in this guide treats a provider-imposed dispute gate as customer cancellation. A payment gate and account closure remain different states.

The guide's replacement notice said legacy exceptions would be reviewed under the 2025 schedule, with negotiated documents checked individually and contractual notice observed. It did not say staff should erase historical evidence or backdate the new rules. Some internal search results still rank this archived guide first because it was frequently referenced. Its familiar wording makes it useful background but unsafe as sole authority for today's action. The current approved procedure and the case-specific decision must be attached to any invoice request. The archived help card should be marked superseded where it remains in support macros, preserving the original for this account's evidence review.
# E06 — Current pricing change and renewal procedure

Record version: PRICE-2025.1. Owner: Revenue Operations. Issued: 2025-03-15. Effective: 2025-04-01 for new orders; existing renewals subject to contract and notice. Status: current operating policy. All business records, people, dialogue and account identifiers in this dossier are synthetic.

The standardized annual Core40 list price is $14,400 excluding tax. This policy applies immediately to new orders signed on or after April 1. Existing negotiated accounts must be checked against their order, any relevant representation, and the applicable notice requirement. A general policy date is not a universal effective date for every customer. For an existing account with a sixty-day price-notice requirement, staff must record the intended renewal boundary and evidence of the prescribed notice before treating the increase as undisputed.

NacreFlow's notice standard distinguishes dispatch, server acceptance, content coverage and human acknowledgment. A mail-service success code can establish that a receiving system accepted a message. It does not prove that a customer read it, that the correct contractual address was used, or that the message described the relevant amount and effective date. A dashboard banner is supplemental unless the applicable agreement makes it the notice channel. Support can report observed evidence without adopting a categorical legal conclusion about effectiveness.

Auto-renewal settings reflect the existing order's renewal mechanism. They do not authorize staff to accept an unexecuted change on the customer's behalf. When a material price dispute remains near renewal, the owner should obtain a duty-lead processing gate or an approved commercial instruction before the automatic batch runs. The gate must state an expiry, service entitlement and follow-up owner. It is not a cancellation, a refund or a silent replacement contract. Leaving a gate to expire without a plan can cause the old automation to resume.

A paid bridge is a separately described short subscription interval. It requires authorized customer acceptance of price, dates, service scope and what happens at its end. Staff must not call a bridge free if it has a charge or imply that accepting it resolves permanent-rate claims. A one-year commercial accommodation also requires the necessary provider approval and customer authority. It does not prove the historical letter was invalid or valid. Records should distinguish a without-prejudice operational accommodation from a legally final settlement.

Support must not condition preservation of a disputed claim on purchasing an expansion or deleting public criticism. No standard cancellation fee applies before the pending renewal in this account. Nonrenewal and export can be offered accurately, but a customer expression of dissatisfaction is not enough to close a working account. The owner must record the specific election. If a negotiated resolution is still pending, keep the status open, make the next controlled update, and refer the actual authority issue to the named decision maker. Current policy does not require staff to make an unsupported final legal determination in order to prevent a disputed automatic charge.
# E07 — Notice delivery and contact audit

# E08 — Customer dispute and requested decision timing

Record version: THREAD-2240.3. Owner: Support. Messages: 2025-06-23 through 2025-06-27 09:15 UTC; cross-reference annotation added 2025-06-27 13:30 UTC. Status: authenticated correspondence. All business records, people, dialogue and account identifiers in this dossier are synthetic.

She says a surprise fifty percent rise would require repricing work already promised to clients. She does not claim a legal right to free expansion. Her board's budget meeting is June 30 at 15:00. She does not promise the board will approve a new annual term. Noor can run exports but wants to avoid a change during those submissions. He is willing to remove unused contractor invitations if it helps scope a future option. The thread contains no acceptance of the three-month bridge or the new $14,400 annual price. # E09 — Billing ledger and pending automation

Record version: BILL-2240.4. Owner: Finance Operations specialist Jules Ferris. Snapshot: 2025-06-27 12:50 UTC. Status: verified ledger and job state, not completed gate. All business records, people, dialogue and account identifiers in this dossier are synthetic.

# E10 — Service scope, usage and expansion requests

Record version: PROD-2240.2. Owner: Product Operations lead Dara Vale. Recorded: 2025-06-26 16:00 UTC. Status: verified current configuration and limited fit analysis. All business records, people, dialogue and account identifiers in this dossier are synthetic.

Rookfield has forty paid staff seats, thirty-seven active staff accounts and three reserved positions. Six invited contractors remain read-only reviewers. The service's new user interface calls all sixty-three visible participants collaborators, including archived reviewers. That dashboard count is not a count of paid staff seats and does not show breach of the purchased quantity. Sales' forty-eight-seat proposal adds capacity that has not yet been requested by an authorized commercial signatory.

Noor discussed a possible autumn expansion of eight staff seats during a May product demonstration. He requested an estimate, stating that two future client projects might need dedicated coordinators. No start date, quantity election or purchase order followed. The demonstration enabled a read-only feature preview in a separate sandbox; it did not provision the paid Analytics module. Technical staff confirm that production remains Core40 with the same API, project limits and export features as the last paid year. The pricing change is not forced by a current technical need to upgrade.

The API is used by two transport-planning workflows for nightly status exchange. Their traffic is comfortably within Core40's allowance. A lower-priced new tier called Team30 is limited to thirty named staff and lacks scheduled API exports. Moving to it would require account cleanup, revised workflows and an explicit decision about seven active staff. It is not a harmless way to keep the invoice near the prior annual amount. A three-month Core40 bridge would keep the existing service configuration and included capabilities. It would not include the proposed eight additional seats, Analytics, custom implementation support or a permanent price lock. Product Operations can continue ordinary support and help test exports during that period. It cannot guarantee that every external integration remains unchanged forever. Planned interface maintenance in August does not remove the existing API; that separate change notice is unrelated to the rate dispute and should not be misrepresented as a retirement deadline.

Dara can provide a verified current-seat report and a sample project export by June 30 11:00. The report will distinguish staff, reviewers and archived users. A representative export includes project fields, attachments and status history, but linked files stored in Rookfield's own drive remain external references. The existing API permits a larger scheduled export if Noor authorizes it. Product Operations will not access the contents of unrelated client projects just to recommend a sales tier. Any future commercial comparison should use actual staff needs and workflow requirements, not the misleading collaborator total from the redesigned dashboard.
# E11 — Renewal sales correspondence and incentive record

# E12 — Continuity, nonrenewal and export procedure

Record version: CONT-2025.2. Owner: Customer Operations. Effective: 2025-05-01. Case assessment: 2025-06-27 11:00 UTC. Status: current service operations procedure. All business records, people, dialogue and account identifiers in this dossier are synthetic.

A manual renewal gate preserves the existing Core40 entitlement for its recorded period. It prevents the automatic renewal workflow from deciding the disputed price while a responsible owner resolves the next instruction. Under the duty-lead delegation, up to seven calendar days of this continuity beyond the paid boundary can be provided without a new charge; the processing gate can be entered before that boundary. This is a processing accommodation, not a fresh annual sale. It does not close projects, reduce staff count or cancel Rookfield's existing order. The gate's expiry must be set deliberately because the batch engine otherwise retries queued work.

When a customer elects a paid bridge, Finance must replace the annual draft with the approved short-period schedule and record that the annual renewal path is not to resume at gate expiry. Customer Operations verifies that service entitlement covers the accepted bridge dates. The bridge's end does not authorize automatic conversion to the $14,400 annual plan. A separate election must define what follows. At least ten calendar days before bridge expiry, the owner must contact the commercial signatory with accurate options and transition implications.

An authorized nonrenewal instruction can stop the upcoming annual term. It must specify whether full production access ends at the paid boundary, a separately approved bridge ends later, or an export interval is requested. Nonrenewal is different from immediate deletion. Immediate account cancellation removes ordinary user access and can interrupt active workflows, so it must not be inferred from a disputed price or a request to stop an automatic charge. The archive-retention schedule is thirty days from actual account closure; a dispute gate does not start that clock.

Standard exports include projects and uploaded attachments. External-drive files remain links, and users need their own access to retrieve them. Export ownership rests with Noor, with Support coordinating verification of a sample. Staff should not promise complete migration from file generation alone. Rookfield's integration owners need to validate mapping of project identifiers and scheduled jobs in any replacement system. Customer Operations estimates two working days for a full export job after authorized scoping, subject to unusually large attachments. No guarantee of a complete competitor migration by July 1 is supported.

A reduced tier can only follow a clear scope and impact review. Team30 would remove capabilities Rookfield currently uses and has fewer seats than active staff. The product's public list price is not evidence of customer consent to that downgrade. Any proposal must state what will stop, when, and what preparation is needed.
